name: Santorini
keyfacts: Vines are trained in a basket system called kouloura, and the grapes ripen inside the baskets, protected from the strong winds.
Phylloxera never reached the island, which is credited to its sandy volcanic soil, so the vines grow on their own roots and some may be 300 years old.
The soils are sandy mixes of pumice and ash, very low in clay and organic matter, and the island has strong summer winds and about ⟦rain|10 to 15 inches|250 to 380 mm⟧ of rain a year.
Dry Santorini must be at least 85% Assyrtiko, with the rest Athiri and Aidani.
Vinsanto must be at least 51% Assyrtiko, made from grapes sun-dried for 7 to 12 days, and aged at least 24 months in oak.

notes: Santorini Assyrtiko is bone dry and full bodied, with high acidity, citrus, stone fruit and a distinct minerality.
Low-yielding vines in volcanic ash give concentrated wines with briny salinity and razor-sharp acidity.
Vinsanto, from sun-dried grapes, is golden orange to amber, with dried apricot, golden raisin, sweet spice and minerality.

blurb.text: A Cycladic island in the Aegean Islands group whose wines, above all Vinsanto, were counted among the great wines of the Aegean under Venetian rule. The PDO centers on white grapes such as Assyrtiko, Athiri and Aidani Aspro, and covers dry wine, fortified wine and Vinsanto, made from sun-dried grapes.
